quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if you can.
Stay seated and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep the motorcycle straight. Just before you hit it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to riding during the day, a rider should do all of the following except:

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Keep more space between their motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use their high beam whenever possible.
Tailgate other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgate other vehicles.
questions.explanation: To stay safe when riding at night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: When braking on a surface with poor traction, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brakes harder than usual.
Apply the brakes gently.
Do not use the rear brake.
Do not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: On surfaces with poor traction, use caution and apply the brakes gently when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Only a front brake.
Only a rear brake.
Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
Three brakes: front, rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time. Press them firmly and do not panic if they lock up.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the flat tire.
Apply both brakes.
Do not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If one tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the good tire (if you are sure which one it is).

questions.question: As a beginning rider, how far should you stay behind another vehicle?

options.text: At least a four-second distance.
Get as close as possible.
Do not worry about your distance behind them.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so they can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least a four-second distance.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least a four-second distance from the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with arms fully stretched out.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing, keep your headlight on all the time, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while taking a curve is usually caused by:

options.text: Taking the turn too fast.
Lanes that are too narrow.
Not knowing how to steer.
Lanes that are too wide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Entering a curve too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road completely.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes and let them pass when it is safe to do so. Speeding up may make the danger worse by causing them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Help you avoid traffic signals.
Communicate your intentions to other road users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and surface hazards. It stops other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Begin slowing sooner than usual.
Begin slowing later than usual.
Apply the brakes more firmly than usual to stop quickly.
Apply the brakes more softly than usual to keep from overworking them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger in a sidecar changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more space to stop completely.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: All of the following will lessen your chances of an accident, except:

options.text: Remaining alert.
Identifying hazards and prioritizing risks.
Riding without a headlight.
Maintaining a space cushion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To reduce your risk of a crash, stay alert and ready to react. Identify hazards and decide which ones to address first. Always use your headlight to be more visible and keep enough space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop until the animal loses interest.
Swerve around the animal.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If a dog is chasing you, slow down and approach it at a slow speed. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Increase your ability to be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen by others. It keeps you out of other drivers' blind spots, helps you avoid surface hazards, protects your lane from other drivers, shows your intentions to others, helps you avoid wind blasts, and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: If you are riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Stay in a lane position that makes you visible to the driver.
Always ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Not be concerned about your placement.
Always ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a lane position that makes you visible to the driver.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, ride in the center portion of your lane. This position makes you most visible in the rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When you ride a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help maintain balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: A helmet will not provide the best possible protection if:

options.text: It is certified by the DOT.
It fits snugly.
It is free of defects.
It has cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has cracks.
questions.explanation: A helmet should meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards and fit snugly all the way around for maximum protection. It should have no defects such as cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire goes flat while you are riding?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the bike straight. Brake slowly on the good tire only. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: A person is considered legally intoxicated at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: For people age 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means they are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride any vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only when riding on wet pavement.
Use both brakes every time, no matter what.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes every time, no matter what.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders ride?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they feel most comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride right behind the leader near the front of the group. This lets experienced riders in the back watch over them.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a pyramid formation.
One at a time.
In a splintered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing. Continue this way until all riders have safely passed.
